key_insight: A single shared low-rank LoRA subspace can be incrementally adapted so new tasks are learned with task-specific low-dimensional coefficients, enabling almost-strict continual learning without replay or multiple adapters while keeping parameter cost low.
problem_solved: Reduces catastrophic forgetting and the computational/storage burden of adapting large pretrained models to many sequential tasks, removing the need for data replay or a separate adapter per task.
method: Learn a shared low-rank LoRA subspace and represent each task by compact coefficients projected into that subspace instead of training independent adapters.
Adaptively expand or refine the shared subspace only when necessary and apply constraints (e.g., orthogonality/regularization) to protect previously acquired knowledge and reduce interference.
Keep a single adapter plus small task embeddings, minimizing extra parameters and compute for continual adaptation without replay.
impact: Makes continual adaptation of large models practical and lightweight for real-world systems—lowering storage, compute and management overhead while preserving task performance across long sequences of tasks.
visual_elements: Diagram contrasting multiple per-task adapters vs one shared LoRA subspace with task-specific coefficient vectors projecting into it.
Line chart showing accuracy across a task sequence: Share (shared-subspace) vs per-task LoRA vs naive finetuning (illustrating reduced forgetting).
Bar chart comparing parameter/storage cost per task (Share vs per-task adapters vs full finetuning).
Flowchart of the training loop: receive new task → project into shared subspace → adapt coefficients / expand basis → apply regularizer to preserve old tasks.
paper_title: Shared LoRA Subspaces for almost Strict Continual Learning
paper_authors: Prakhar Kaushik, Ankit Vaidya, Shravan Chaudhari, Rama Chellappa, Alan Yuille
